Chambishi Copper Smelter Ltd Reports Steady Output and Revenue Growth in Latest Results

Chambishi Copper Smelter Ltd, one of Zambia’s prominent copper processing facilities, reported stable financial and operational performance in its latest quarterly results, reflecting persistent demand and resilient production amid a volatile international market for base metals.

According to figures released on Thursday, Chambishi Copper Smelter Ltd processed 62,400 metric tonnes of copper concentrate during the quarter ending March 31, marking a 4.2% increase from the same period last year. The company posted revenue of $143 million, up 6% year-on-year, supported by a moderate rise in copper prices and improved operational efficiency.

“We are pleased with our consistent production levels and sustained earnings,” General Manager Benson Mwansa said in a statement. “Our operational team has maintained high standards of safety and efficiency, allowing us to navigate challenges in the global supply chain and fluctuating commodity markets.”

Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) for the period reached $38.5 million, compared to $36.1 million a year earlier. Net profit stood at $15.4 million, up from $14.2 million in the prior year, driven by stable output and ongoing cost-optimization initiatives.

Copper, Zambia’s principal export, has seen renewed investor interest amid global electrification trends. Industry analysts say Chambishi Copper Smelter Ltd has benefited from robust demand in Asia, particularly for copper cathodes used in electronics and infrastructure projects. “Chambishi’s latest results underscore Zambia’s ability to maintain reliable supply to international markets,” said Alice Chirwa, metals analyst at Frontier Trade Partners. “Their steady performance is a positive signal for the sector and for Zambian export revenues.”

Company officials also highlighted recent investments in plant maintenance and environmental controls, with capital expenditure for the quarter totaling $6.3 million. “We remain committed to minimizing our environmental footprint and supporting the local workforce,” added Mwansa.

Employment at the smelter remained stable at 1,170 staff, with no reported disruptions during the period. The company confirmed it continues to engage with local suppliers and community initiatives in the Copperbelt region.

Looking ahead, Chambishi Copper Smelter Ltd projects continued stable operations, with management focused on process improvements and disciplined cost management. The company did not provide specific financial guidance for the remainder of the year.
